checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in AZ
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Arizona ROC-licensed HVAC contractor pulls the permit on the owner's behalf — the contractor's ROC license number must appear on the application. For this scope, the relevant Arizona classification is CR-67 (refrigeration) for HVAC work.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to City of Tempe Community Development Building Safety

common_mistakes: Starting rooftop demo before the permit is issued and posted — Tempe can stop the job and require re-submittal
Assuming same tonnage means no permit — commercial HVAC replacement still needs a mechanical permit
Not verifying rooftop curb dimensions and unit footprint before ordering the replacement unit
Failing to confirm whether the existing electrical disconnect, whip, or gas connection can be reused without modification

Submitting permit application without verifying current contractor registration status — an expired or lapsed city registration will block your application silently. Verify your registration is current BEFORE submitting.

pro_tips: Have the rooftop unit submittal sheet ready before you open the permit application — Tempe reviewers move faster when tonnage, voltage, and curb dimensions are already documented.
If the crane pick is part of the job, line up the lift date after permit issuance so you do not pay twice for mobilization.
Check your Tempe contractor registration renewal date before starting any permit application — registration lapses are the #1 avoidable rejection reason.
For rooftop replacements, photograph the existing curb, disconnect, and gas/electrical tie-in before removal; it helps resolve inspector questions if the field conditions differ from the plans.

response_body.zoning_hoa_flag: Commercial rooftop equipment can still be affected by zoning, rooftop screening, historic district overlays, or landlord/tenant design review. If the building is in a historic district or has rooftop screening requirements, verify whether the new unit visibility, curb height, or screening changes need separate approval before installation.
